projects.name: promptflip
projects.tagline: A fun way to versus my friends: two prompts, two OpenRouter keys, and a provably fair coin flip decides whose prompt gets answered and whose key pays.

projects.name: Basketball Stat Tracker
projects.tagline: Counts makes, misses and streaks from the mini hoop in my room.

projects.name: Plato
projects.tagline: Give it your course outlines and it pulls every assignment and deadline into one calendar file, because I was tired of doing that by hand every semester.

projects.name: Plant It
projects.tagline: Yash and I built a plant waterer that identifies your plant from a photo, looks up its care, and waters each plant to its own soil-moisture level.

projects.name: Pushup Form Tracker
projects.tagline: My first AI project: Yash and I gathered our own pushup data, trained a model on it, and now the webcam counts your reps and grades your form in the browser.

projects.name: Emote Detector
projects.tagline: I love Clash Royale and wanted to do more computer vision, so your webcam gestures fire Clash Royale emotes, sound included.

projects.name: Microtubule Quantification
projects.tagline: Nobody could point me to an industry-standard way to quantify microtubules from immunofluorescence images for a class project, so I built one that runs in your browser.

projects.name: UnPark — Parkinson's freeze detection
projects.tagline: Built for a competition: a haptic ankle device that catches freezing-of-gait episodes in Parkinson's with an accelerometer and logs them straight to your phone.

projects.name: Automatic RC Car
projects.tagline: A small RC car we built: drive it with a PS4 controller, or switch it to self-driving and it follows any green tennis ball you throw, using a vision model on its Raspberry Pi.

projects.name: FlashCards
projects.tagline: Under construction: an iPhone flashcard app, nothing to show yet.

projects.name: Porsche PCB keychain
projects.tagline: One of my first PCB designs, made for Yash's birthday: a keychain-sized board with a Porsche cut through it, USB-C, and three LEDs underneath so the Porsche glows when you plug it into your phone.

projects.name: DIY EEG
projects.tagline: Under construction: a home-built EEG front end; the schematic and LTspice simulation are done, the board and firmware are next.

projects.name: Sift
projects.tagline: The two or three papers from this week that are actually worth reading.
